Attached are NovaMed's initial redlines to the MSA + Order Form with a focus on the security exhibit and audit rights. A few specifics to call out up-front so we can align quickly:

- SOC 2: we require the latest SOC 2 Type II report on an annual cadence and a 30-day window for remediation confirmations if the report flags any control gaps.

Hi Melissa — thanks for the redlines. I reviewed the document and flagged the clauses that will likely require negotiation. High-level summary below and attached a marked-up MSA to this thread.

Key legal points:
- Broad audit/inspection clause: Your current wording grants unlimited on-demand inspection. We propose a scoped audit right tied to specific SOC 2 assertions and a documented evidence request process. This protects both parties and keeps requests time-boxed.
- Pen test notice and delivery of findings: We are open to an external pen-test but will need a clearly defined notice window and a non-disclosure/confidentiality process for findings. 10 business days is workable if the test is scoped and scheduled; for live testing we enforce a blackout list for critical infrastructure.
- Evidence retention & PII: We cannot produce raw customer data or PII. Any artifact sets we provide will be sanitized/aggregated. We propose a standard evidence workbook that lists acceptable artifacts and a cadence for delivery (we proposed 30 days from request for most items).

Proposed compromises in the attached:
- Replace unlimited audit rights with: scoped audit rights (SOC 2 attestation review; 1 on-site or remote inspection per 12-month period, with 15 business days' notice).
- Pen-test: agree to 10 business days' notice for scheduled external tests against staging; internal pen-tests require 5 business days' notice. Findings deliverable: high-level executive summary + technical appendix shared under NDA.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly evidence windows for pre-agreed artifact sets; ad-hoc requests to follow the evidence request workflow with a 30-day turnaround.

I've copied Priyom in case there are contract-level exceptions we should consider for enterprise procurement.

[Attachment: rdw-MSA_marked_20261102.pdf]

Happy to walk through these points on tomorrow's call.

Laura Bennett

Thanks everyone — adding the technical detail below so Melissa and NovaMed Legal have clarity before we lock language.

Pen-test operating model (recommended):
- Staging-first approach: tests to run on a dedicated staging tenant that mirrors production config but contains synthetic/test data. Live production tests allowed only under explicit, documented exceptions and with a mutually agreed rollback plan.
- Notice windows: 10 business days for external vendors against staging (to allow scheduling and provisioning); internal scheduled tests: 5 business days.
- Allowed activity: vulnerability scanning, authenticated testing with scoped accounts, and targeted exploit validation. Full destructive testing is prohibited.
- IP allowlist & monitoring: provide a vendor IP range and testing schedule; we will whitelist for the test window and monitor in real time. Any anomalous activity will trigger an immediate pause.

Evidence artifacts (what we can reasonably provide):
- SOC 2 report (redacted as necessary for customer-specific data) — annual delivery.
- Infrastructure diagrams, network ACL screenshots, and role-based access control snapshots — provided in an evidence workbook.
- Aggregated auth/access logs covering the request window — exported in CSV with a 30-day lead time for ad-hoc requests.

Operational asks from NovaMed to make cadence workable:
1) Narrow the artifact set per quarter (we can pre-agree a list for Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4).
2) Provide a single evidence intake ticket per window with the requested artifact checklist.
3) For pen-tests, share vendor scope and testing plan at T-minus 5 business days so we can confirm staging readiness.

I've attached our evidence ops playbook and a draft evidence matrix. If those are acceptable we can bake them into the exhibit as an appendix rather than putting details into the MSA body.

[Attachment: evidence-ops-playbook.pdf]
[Attachment: rdw-evidence-matrix-draft.xlsx]

Karthik Iyer
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
